The prophets
The kings

The people, the priests, and the Levites
Only the priests and Levites

He celebrated
He tore his garments and sat astonished

easy.q: How did Ezra react when he heard the report?

answers: The princes and rulers were chief in the trespass
It happened only outside Jerusalem
It lasted for only one day
medium.explanation: Ezra 9:2 says, “the hand of the princes and rulers hath been chief in this trespass.”
medium.q: What made the intermarriage especially serious according to the report?

answers: Very joyful
Shocked and deeply distressed
Ready to depart
medium.explanation: “Astonied” describes Ezra as stunned and overwhelmed by grief.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “astonied” mean in these verses?

answers: They trembled at the words of the God of Israel
They wanted to become princes
They had heard of a military victory
medium.explanation: The people gathered because they trembled at the words of the God of Israel.
medium.q: Why did additional people gather around Ezra?

answers: The leaders were setting a bad example for the people
The leaders did not know the commandments
The leaders had left Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The report emphasizes that the leaders were foremost in the wrongdoing, making their influence especially serious.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the princes and rulers being chief in the trespass?

answers: Preparation for war
Joy over the people’s return
Deep mourning and shock
challenge.explanation: These actions immediately followed the troubling report and showed Ezra’s profound grief.
challenge.q: What did Ezra’s tearing of his garments and pulling out his hair express?

They gathered to stop Ezra from praying
The princes commanded them to gather
challenge.explanation: The passage presents Ezra sitting astonished, followed by the gathering of those who trembled at God’s words.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between Ezra’s reaction and the gathering of the people who trembled?

paragraphs.title: The Confession and Recognition of Guilt

answers: In the morning
At the evening sacrifice
At midnight
easy.explanation: Ezra 9:5 says, “at the evening sacrifice I arose up from my heaviness.”
easy.q: When did Ezra rise from his heaviness?

answers: He fell upon his knees and spread out his hands
He stood on the wall
He sat and ate
easy.explanation: Ezra fell upon his knees and spread out his hands unto the LORD.
easy.q: What did Ezra do while praying?

answers: The nation’s military strength
God’s grace and the remnant that escaped
The wealth of the kings of the land
easy.explanation: Ezra remembered that God had left them a remnant, given them reviving, and helped them rebuild.
easy.q: What did Ezra mention alongside the people’s guilt?

answers: Only the princes
The people and their fathers’ generations
Only the priests
medium.explanation: Ezra said, “Since the days of our fathers have we been in a great trespass.”
medium.q: For whom did Ezra include himself in his confession?

answers: A surviving remainder
A newly built city
A valuable gift
medium.explanation: A remnant is a small group that remains or survives.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “remnant” mean in verse 8?

answers: God gave them only a new king
God preserved a remnant, gave them reviving, and helped restore Jerusalem
God abolished all the commandments
medium.explanation: The passage mentions a remnant, reviving, the house of God, and a wall in Judah and Jerusalem.
medium.q: How is God’s grace described in verses 8–9?

answers: To show that the people were guilty but had still received mercy
To claim that the people had not sinned
To describe only the success of the rebuilding
challenge.explanation: Ezra confesses their guilt while remembering that God had not forsaken them.
challenge.q: Why does Ezra’s prayer include both confession of sin and remembrance of God’s grace?

answers: God gave the people stability and a secure place
God commanded the people to leave the land
God gave them only a tool for construction
challenge.explanation: The image of a nail suggests something fixed, secure, and established in the holy place.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the phrase “to give us a nail in his holy place”?

answers: Guilt, remembrance of grace, and recognition of God’s help
Victory, celebration, and preparation for war
Building, dividing property, and appointing a king
challenge.explanation: Ezra begins with confession and then recalls God’s mercy and help through the kings of Persia.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in Ezra’s prayer?

paragraphs.title: Violation of the Commandments and Fear of Losing the Remnant

answers: Their land
God’s commandments
Their work
easy.explanation: Ezra says, “we have forsaken thy commandments.”
easy.q: What had the people forsaken according to Ezra?

answers: Not to give their daughters to their sons or take their daughters for their sons
Not to speak with the people of the lands
Not to work their fields
easy.explanation: The instruction prohibited forming marriages with the people of the lands.
easy.q: What command was given concerning the people of the lands?

answers: With a declaration of victory
By acknowledging God’s righteousness and the people’s guilt
With a request to the king of Persia
easy.explanation: Ezra says, “O LORD God of Israel, thou art righteous,” while confessing their trespasses.
easy.q: How does Ezra end his prayer?

answers: Because God had already shown them great mercy and goodness
Because the people had no leaders
Because the land was empty
medium.explanation: Ezra remembers the remnant, the reviving, the restoration of God’s house, and the wall God provided.
medium.q: Why is Ezra troubled by the people’s disobedience?

answers: God punished them more severely than they deserved
God did not destroy them as fully as their sins deserved
God sent them away from the land
medium.explanation: Ezra recognizes that God mercifully withheld the full punishment their sins deserved.
medium.q: What does Ezra mean by saying God had punished them less than their iniquities deserved?

answers: Complete destruction, with no remnant or escape
The loss of the temple only
A shortage of food only
medium.explanation: Ezra asks whether God would consume them so that there would be no remnant nor escaping.
medium.q: What does Ezra fear if the people again break God’s commandments?

answers: Ezra sees continued disobedience as a danger that could bring complete destruction
Ezra believes the prohibition applies only to leaders
Ezra says the prohibition would immediately make the people leave the land
challenge.explanation: After recalling the forbidden relationship with the people of the lands, Ezra fears destruction without a remnant.
challenge.q: How is the prohibition against intermarriage connected to Ezra’s fear of losing the remnant?

answers: The people deserved mercy because they had not sinned
God is righteous, while the people stand before Him in their trespasses
The people are righteous and God owes them an answer
challenge.explanation: Ezra declares God righteous but admits that the people remain guilty before Him.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between God’s character and the people’s condition at the end of the prayer?

answers: The people should not disregard God’s mercy by returning to the same sin
The old warnings should all be cancelled
The people should avoid public prayer
challenge.explanation: Ezra expresses amazement that they could return to disobedience after receiving such mercy and deliverance.
challenge.q: What central idea is expressed by the question, “Should we again break thy commandments”?
